signals.text: Revenue grew 27% a year over 3 years vs 22% over 5: growth is accelerating.
Profit compounded at 20% vs revenue at 27%: profits are lagging sales.

flags.text: Profit compounded at 20% vs revenue at 27%: profits are lagging sales.

guidance.statement: The net interest margins are positioned for a reversal as we enter the upward rate cycle.
guidance.quote: net interest margins, which in recent times has borne the brunt of faster repricing of assets and a lag in cost of funds, in a down rate cycle is also positioned for a reversal as we enter the upward rate cycle.

guidance.statement: Net of FCNR headwinds and rate hike tailwinds, margins are expected to be neutral to positive going forward.
guidance.quote: net of that, we still think that there can be neutral to positive on the margin as we go forward.

delivered.statement: Deposits increased 18.8% year-on-year on a reported basis, including a 4 percentage point lift from FCNR.
Retail disbursements crossed Rs 90,000 crores in Q2 FY27 as against Rs 76,000 crores in Q1.
Asset quality remains pristine with GNPA at 1.11% and credit costs at 44 basis points.
Quarterly PAT was Rs 19.5 billion, a growth of approximately 12.7% excluding trading gains.
Total AUM grew 15.3% year-on-year, including a 1.9% impact of FCNR leverage.
September 26 EOP loan growth for MSME and mid-market grew 23.5% year-on-year.

calls.tone: confident on underlying momentum and asset quality, expecting margin recovery with new leadership

pushback.gist: Analysts questioned why HDFC Bank's margin decline was similar to peers despite lower corporate growth.
Concerned about low LCR and whether branch productivity can sustain liability accretion in a changing market.
Pressed on what is driving cost of funds higher sequentially despite flat aggregate averages.

business.summary: HDFC Bank provides banking and financial services, making money through interest income on retail, MSME, and wholesale loans, fees, and deposits.

segments.name: Retail and MSME / Business Banking
segments.note: Led by expanding retail disbursements and MSME growth.

segments.name: Wholesale / Corporate
segments.note: Calibrated growth focusing on returns and working capital.

guidance.statement: Cost of funds can see a 40 to 50 basis points change, but not in a hurry.
guidance.quote: compared to our historical norms as well as compared to what we have seen in the industry as such, there can be 40, 50 basis points change, but it is not going to change in a hurry.

guidance.statement: Management targets a retail asset mix of around 60% in the long term.
guidance.quote: we were at about 60% or so and we always have thought that India's consumption component of the GDP is at about 60% and that's where we want to be as far as the retail mix is concerned

guidance.statement: Endeavor is to reach a CASA ratio near pre-merger levels of around 38% to 40%.
guidance.quote: the endeavor and our vision is to reach to somewhere near the pre-merger levels or just around the time of the merger, which was around 38.

guidance.statement: Long-term profit growth should be at or above balance sheet growth.
guidance.quote: We do think that in the longer term that the profit growth should be at or above the balance sheet growth.

delivered.statement: Deposit growth continues to be relatively better than historical Q1 trends with market share gains.
Per branch metrics stand at approximately INR 330 crores per branch.
Corporate and wholesale segment advances grew at approximately 18% year-on-year.
MSME business banking segment grew at 22.3% year-on-year.
Disbursements under ECLGS scheme 5.0 reached close to INR 14,000 crores by June 30.
Cost of funds moderated by about 40 basis points year-on-year.

calls.tone: Confident in core franchise resilience and demand, while managing tactical margin and CASA pressures.

pushback.gist: Analysts questioned whether margins have bottomed out and what specific levers remain to recover them.
Repeated concern over the drop in CASA ratio post-merger and whether historical ratios can be restored.
Scepticism on profit growth lagging balance sheet growth significantly over recent periods.
An analyst strongly urged management to move away from Saturday earnings calls to weekday reporting for better global participation.

guidance.statement: Business banking is expected to continue growing in the range of 18% to 20% or 21%.
guidance.quote: and that will continue to also be in that range of 18% to 20%, 21%, depending upon, obviously, some of the developments in the economy.

delivered.statement: System credit growth was 12%, up from 5.5% last year, showing positive momentum.
Deposit growth rate came in at 14.4%, continuing to grow faster than credit growth.
Return on assets continued to be stable at 1.9% (or 1.94% for full year).
Cost-to-income declined from 40.5% to 39.5% on a core basis.
Gross NPAs remained extremely healthy at 1.15%.
Capital position remained strong at 19.7%.

calls.tone: Confident on core franchise, resilient balance sheet, and long-term tech investments while navigating geopolitical and rate uncertainties.

pushback.gist: Analysts questioned whether HDFC Bank's 12% growth is lagging behind the higher industry average.
Concerns were raised about how much of the strong period-end deposit surge is transitory or sustainable.
Analysts pressed on why NIMs haven't benefited more despite shrinking borrowings and rate cuts.
Scepticism regarding tepid growth in third-party distribution fees compared to customer growth.

guidance.statement: Outpace loan growth in the coming year FY27, growing a couple of percentage points above system.
guidance.quote: outpacing loan growth in the coming year in FY '27, as we had sort of mentioned to you all along for the last 18 months.

guidance.statement: Achieve a loan-to-deposit ratio of 85% to 90% by FY27.
guidance.quote: land somewhere around the 85% to 90% for FY '27.

guidance.statement: Maintain loan-to-deposit ratio in the range of 90% to 96% in FY26.
guidance.quote: try and be in a range of somewhere between 90% to 96% in the year FY '26

delivered.statement: Loan-to-deposit ratio glide path continued downwards toward targets.
Cost of funds moved down by about 10 to 11 basis points during the quarter.
Liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) reported at 116 for the quarter.
Agri regulatory inspection impacts of about 5 billion were absorbed in December.
Added about 1 to 1.5 million new liability relationships during the quarter.

calls.tone: Optimistic on credit demand and loan growth acceleration, confident on sustainable downward glide path for LDR.

pushback.gist: Analysts questioned the feasibility of lowering LDR to 90% given current slower deposit growth rates.
Scepticism over the high estimated employee cost impact from the new labor code compared to peers.
Questions raised on why underlying credit costs remain around 55 bps despite stable and low slippages.
Inquiry into why strong market share in spends is not translating into higher card receivables.

guidance.statement: RBI estimates India's GDP growth at 6.6 per cent for fiscal 2026-27.
guidance.quote: The RBI estimates India’s GDP growth at 6.6 per cent and inflation at 5.1 per cent for fiscal 2026-27.

guidance.statement: RBI expects inflation to inch up towards 5.1 per cent in FY 2026-27.
guidance.quote: inflation is expected to inch up towards 5.1 per cent on account of the energy shock.

delivered.statement: India's GDP growth was estimated at 7.7 per cent in the Financial Year 2025-26.
Headline retail inflation averaged 2.1 per cent during FY 2025-26.
System credit growth stood at 14.1 per cent at the end of fiscal 2025-26.
System deposit growth improved meaningfully to 11.5 per cent in fiscal 2025-26.

calls.tone: Optimistic and resilient, highlighting strong domestic demand and growth amidst global challenges.
